title: Hank Williams and Tony Almerico's radio broadcasts
summary: Jones and Allen talk about Hank Williams and the Grand Ole Opry visit, then Tony Almerico's radio shows from the Parisian Room.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It probably did, yeah. Did you ever listen to Hank Williams, correct?
Sure. Hank Williams is one of my favorite songwriters and singers, oh, I love him, yes.
Yeah, well you've been to that your father like country western.
Uh, I can remember when the Grand Ole Opry used to come to New Orleans on a street.

They would perform in a municipal auditorium and I went once with a friend of the family's. And I met, uh, his last wife. They were married here. One of the ceremonies were here in the auditorium. I didn't go to the ceremony, but I met her at Tony Almarico's on the, uh, radio program, the radio station. But yeah, I loved Hank Williams.
Would Tony broadcast remote from the Parisian room or did you go to the station?

Tony had a five-day-a-week radio broadcast from the station that he played. He was a disc jockey. And then he had, gosh, it must have been about three broadcasts. Let's see, he had one on WWL and then he had, uh, one on WJMR, which was a station that he broadcast from, uh, disc jockey. And then he had a third one for the Armed Forces Network or something like that. So he did, spent the best part of his Sunday afternoons doing radio broadcasts, all from the Parisian room.

Yeah, well I can remember JMR and I would go in there to see him. He did his own commercials and played records. That's right. And I'd lend him some of my records from time to time. Uh-huh. I was working for Mercury Records, you know. Or William B. Allen, who was the distributor. Uh-huh. I could sort of check those dates out sometime, but I imagine there was plenty of documentation. Do you have any brothers and sisters?
